LESSON: SAUM

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Devotional Acts
Topic 4.4: Saum

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Saum. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What virtues do Muslims learn from fasting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. apply the virtues acquired from observing saum in day-to-day life
2. appreciate observing saum as an act of ibadah

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SAUM
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Saum helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: SAUM
Study Saum like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Apply the virtues acquired from observing saum in day-to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to apply the virtues acquired from observing saum in day-to-day life. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply the virtues acquired from observing saum in day-to-day life.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Saum” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply the virtues acquired from observing saum in day-to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate observing saum as an act of ibadah

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate observing saum as an act of ibadah. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate observing saum as an act of ibadah.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Saum in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate observing saum as an act of ibadah. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Saum is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Saum” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply the virtues acquired from observing saum in day-to-day life)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Saum in your own words. (skill: appreciate observing saum as an act of ibadah)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Saum to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: apply the virtues acquired from observing saum in day-to-day life.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate observing saum as an act of ibadah.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Saum from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Saum: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Saum?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What virtues do Muslims learn from fasting?
2. What is the significance of fasting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Saum means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: apply the virtues acquired from observing saum in day-to-day life.
5. Be able to: appreciate observing saum as an act of ibadah.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
